prohibited_recommendations: Do not delay treatment awaiting full antibody panels.
Do not give corticosteroids as monotherapy.
required_recommendations: Continuous cardiac telemetry for autonomic features.
Send ganglioside panel and consider paraneoplastic / Sjögren serology if presentation atypical.

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, severe AIDP with sensory ataxia (post-URI)

differential.key_features: Sensory predominance and ataxia; serology (SSA/SSB) and onconeural antibodies; pure sensory neuronopathy typically lacks demyelinating EMG.
Ataxia + areflexia overlap; absence of ophthalmoplegia argues against classic MFS; anti-GQ1b useful.
Cannot exclude at <8 weeks; reassess longitudinally.
Subacute, chronic; B12 level and methylmalonic acid testing; areflexia possible but CSF protein and demyelinating EMG redirect to GBS.
MRI excludes structural cause; sensory level absent.

key_clinical_evidence: Sensory-ataxic GBS variant exists; elevated CSF protein and demyelinating EMG anchor the diagnosis.
Sensory ataxia raises differentiation with paraneoplastic / Sjögren ganglionopathy — broader serology when atypical.

sequence_constraints.reason: Document respiratory status (FVC/NIF) before committing to IVIG vs plasma exchange — severe respiratory compromise mandates ICU triage and may influence treatment choice and timing.
Renal function, IgA screen, and CBC must be reviewed before IVIG to mitigate renal failure, anaphylaxis (IgA-deficient patients), and aseptic meningitis risk.

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL nerve conduction study. 1. Markedly prolonged distal motor latencies bilaterally (peroneal 7.2 ms, tibial 7.8 ms, median 6.4 ms). 2. Severely reduced motor conduction velocities bilaterally (peroneal 28 m/s, tibial 26 m/s, median 38 m/s) with reduced CMAPs. 3. Absent sural SNAPs bilaterally; severely reduced median SNAP (6 µV). 4. Absent F-waves all nerves bilaterally; absent H-reflex bilaterally. 5. Delayed blink reflex: absent R1, delayed R2 — indicating proximal facial nerve conduction slowing. Pattern consistent with severe mixed demyelinating polyneuropathy with conduction block

quantitative_data.pattern: Severe mixed demyelinating polyneuropathy with conduction block; absent F-waves all nerves — acquired demyelinating (AIDP) electrodiagnostic pattern

patient.chief_complaint: Sudden temperature sensation loss followed by progressive lower limb instability, weakness, diplopia, and circumoral numbness — preceded by URI.

social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife and two children

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. B. is a 41-year-old civil engineer presenting with a 10-day history of progressive neurological symptoms. He had an upper respiratory tract infection approximately 12 days ago, treated with a macrolide antibiotic, which resolved. On the day symptoms began, he noticed a sudden loss of hot and cold sensation while taking a shower. He then developed progressive instability and weakness in both legs over the following days. He also developed diplopia, blurred vision in both eyes, and lost his sense of taste. He notes circumoral numbness. By day 7 he could no longer stand without support and presented to the emergency department. On initial exam, a temperature sensory deficit appeared to have a T4 level, which prompted emergent MRI spine. He has no bowel or bladder dysfunction and no incontinence. He has no back pain. He has no history of prior neurological symptoms. Serological testing reveals positive IgM antibodies for multiple viruses including CMV, HSV, and EBV — this triple seropositive pattern raised concern for a primary viral meningoencephalitis.

neurological_exam.additional: FVC: 2.4 L (predicted 4.0 L — 60%). NIF: -30 cmH2O. Sensory loss pattern initially appeared to have a T4 level on temperature testing — raising concern for cord lesion. However, subsequent detailed exam shows patchy rather than sharp demarcation, more consistent with large-fiber neuropathy. URI with macrolide antibiotic treatment several days prior to onset.
neurological_exam.coordination: Limb ataxia — finger-nose dysmetric bilaterally. Heel-shin ataxic.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Blurred vision bilaterally — loss of taste. Bilateral subtle facial weakness. Mild dysarthria.
neurological_exam.motor: Symmetric lower extremity weakness: hip flexion 3/5, knee extension 3+/5, ankle dorsiflexion 3/5. Cannot stand without support. Upper extremity 4/5 bilaterally.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Diminished bilateral patellar and Achilles (1+). Trace bilateral biceps. Plantars downgoing.
neurological_exam.sensory: Temperature sensation loss below T4 level — patchy. Pain and light touch relatively preserved distally. Circumoral numbness.
